ESTABLISHED FACTS (verified at audit baseline fc3e2c132/e24d42bf): a live TypeScript consumer launches the bridge (src/cli/src/services/raphael-bridge.ts:32-49; src/cli/src/tools/raphaelTools.ts:2-6; src/cli/package.json raphael:bridge recipe); the bridge and both config shims insert an absent directory at sys.path[0] (/home/yaser/raphael-2.0, verified absent) at raphael_bridge.py:15, config/paths.py:2, config/target.py:2; the four agent.* routes dispatch to module-level handle() functions that do not exist in the agent modules (dead-end routes); 25 weld-table methods are gated fail-closed via enforce_broker_mediation and DENY under bootstrap-v0 on action-type, literal capability membership, and impact; non-weld effect-bearing methods (persona.set, target.set, scope.set, brain.memory_store/recall, conductor.call/select_strategy) carry no bridge-level authorization contract. decision_text: PROPOSED OUTCOME (PROVISIONAL). Carries no authority and confers none; effective only if ratified in this ledger by a named authority principal distinct from the proposer, recorded verbatim. PROPOSED R1 — MANDATORY receipt-to-execution binding, in two components with different authority requirements. (1) CANONICAL RUNTIME — APPLICATION of accepted requirements: ADR-003 INV-2 (every execution event carries the Broker decision_id) and INV-3 (execution-derived claims require receipts), already implemented and tested as the section-14.6 F1 six-dimension binding: src/orchestrator/hardening/action_receipt.py hash-binds target, capability, method, impact, action_type and authorized_argv and tracks STARTED to SUCCEEDED/FAILED/TIMEOUT with evidence_ids; src/orchestrator/runtime/stages.py binds receipts to the mission-scoped action id (RSI-1 Fix A) and persists durable denial records; evidence/g3_remediation/STATUS.md records F1 as IMPLEMENTED + PROVEN. (2) LEGACY WELD PERIMETER — INTERPRETIVE EXTENSION requiring explicit GLM architecture-authority approval before or at ratification: all ~57 enforce_broker_mediation call sites (grep-verified; none captures the return value) discard the returned receipt, and none demonstrates receipt-to-action binding. Extending the binding obligation beyond the documented canonical closure (F2 perimeter record; product-readiness report section 5.2) is not settled by any accepted record; operator ratification alone is INSUFFICIENT for this component. REQUIRED POLICY-LEVEL GUARANTEES: binding of authorized target; capability; method and arguments; execution identity/call-site; terminal status; and evidence linkage via decision_id. EXPLICIT CLARIFICATION: an AUTHORIZED receipt is an authorization-decision artifact only — it does not operationally approve any execution, and no weld site demonstrates that what executed matched what was authorized. REJECTED: R2 (would institutionalize unbound authorization at precisely the sites created to close bypasses). DEPENDENCIES: precedes receipt-lifecycle remediation design; implementation is additionally barred by the P4/RSI freeze (ReceiptStore is P4.4 scope). ENGINEERING: design records only; no implementation authorized.

SCOPE: the three reviewed gates (orchestrator goal gate; exploit per-action gate; postex per-action gate). DEPENDENCIES: governs any change to or reliance on the bypass; correction design (strict parsing; Broker-routed) may proceed as records. RATIFICATION: operator; GLM-awareness note recommended.
